verdict: Caution — lend selectively to downstream fabricators tied to the Jharsuguda aluminium park and to strong smelter-linked service units; avoid standalone traders and small converters with no anchor offtake until Odisha's demand signals improve.
title: Jharsuguda aluminium & products: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**Aluminium here is a power-and-ore conversion business: bauxite and alumina go in, electricity does the heavy lifting, and hot metal or ingots come out to be rolled, extruded or cast downstream.** Cash sits in the smelter's working-capital cycle (alumina and coal inventory, power bills, metal receivables) and, for downstream units, in the conversion spread between metal cost and finished-product price. **Pricing power is thin for small converters — they pass metal price through and earn a conversion margin — so when a proposal lands, check whether the borrower earns a fixed conversion fee or is speculating on metal price; if the latter, ask for the hedging policy.**

## What has changed now
**The anchor is expanding: Vedanta announced a ₹1 lakh crore Odisha programme including a brownfield expansion of its one-million-tonne-per-annum Jharsuguda smelter [1][2], and a ₹500 crore aluminium park at Jharsuguda has already signed MoUs with two manufacturing units [3].** That is real downstream demand for fabricators, but it is an announcement, not yet cash flow — **so when a proposal lands citing park tenancy, check the signed allotment and offtake letter, not the press release.** Peer results are strong: Vedanta Aluminium's Q2FY27 revenue rose 41% YoY to ₹22,066 crore with EBITDA up 83% [4], and profit more than doubled on record production of 649,000 metric tons [6]. **But management guided net effective price in H2 about $50 lower than Q2 [5] — treat the margin peak as past, not as the borrower's base case.**

## The local demand signal is the caution
**Odisha's GST collections grew 0.5% Apr-to-date against India's 6.1%, and electricity demand grew 5.1% against India's 9.5% [D] — the state is running well behind the country.** India-wide aluminium output (NIC 24) grew 2.4% YoY [D]. **So the smelter's own numbers are healthy while the surrounding state economy is soft; lend to the supply chain of the strong anchor, not to the general local market.** An ICRA note (dated August 2025, over a year old) flags margin sensitivity to international aluminium prices and logistics [10]; use it as background only.

## How to grow safely
**Pursue downstream fabricators with a Vedanta park allotment, extruders and casters with anchor offtake, and service units (fabrication, transport, maintenance) with purchase orders from the smelter.** Avoid standalone metal traders and small converters selling into the soft Odisha market without a contracted buyer. **Structure against conversion margin, not metal price: keep drawing power on stock-and-debtor statements, take a monthly stock statement and quarterly GST returns, and covenant a minimum interest-coverage floor.** For any borrower citing the ₹1 lakh crore plan [1][2], **ask for the phased capex schedule and their own signed contract — collect from customer.**

## Early-warning signs
**Watch for receivable days stretching past the borrower's stated terms, conversion-fee realisation falling below the sanctioned rate, and inventory building without matching orders.** Any borrower whose sales are concentrated in one anchor should report that anchor's payment behaviour monthly. **If GST turnover for the borrower's district slips for two quarters, cut limits before renewal.**
watch: Receivable days exceed stated terms by 15 days -> freeze drawing power and seek fresh offtake proof
Order book drops or anchor payment delays -> downgrade internal rating and raise margin
Coverage falls below covenanted floor -> demand promoter support or restructure
watch_note: Trigger levels are policy suggestions (analytical framing), not data.
news_why: Odisha GST and power demand growth lag India sharply, outweighing strong anchor results.
